title: NASA releases image of Mars and Beehive cluster under aurora
excerpt: The photograph was captured near Lansjärv, Sweden, following a solar eruption on October 10, 2026.
bodyHtml:
NASA published an image on October 14, 2026, showing Mars and the Beehive cluster, also known as M44 or Praesepe, positioned beneath an auroral curtain. The photograph was taken near Lansjärv, Sweden.

According to NASA, an eruption off the Sun reached Earth on October 10, 2026, causing disturbances in the magnetic field. These disturbances resulted in energetic particles colliding with atmospheric molecules to create the aurora.

At the time of the capture, Mars appeared closest to the center of the Beehive cluster. The Beehive cluster is a swarm of young stars. Their rotation periods have helped humanity learn about how stars spin slower over time as they lose mass through their stellar winds.
